name: Non-hereditary Late-Onset Primary Lymphedema

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Lymphedema

criteria.description: Chronic, progressive unilateral or bilateral limb swelling persisting for more than 3 months
Exclusion of secondary causes of lymphedema such as infection, malignancy, trauma, or surgery
Onset of lymphedema symptoms after puberty (late-onset)
Imaging confirmation of lymphatic dysfunction by lymphoscintigraphy or equivalent
No family history of lymphedema or hereditary lymphatic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: chronic limb swelling >3 months, exclusion of secondary causes, and onset after puberty
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical, supported by imaging and exclusion of secondary causes. Genetic testing typically negative.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic non-pitting edema of the lower limb
pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects one or both legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Stemmer sign (inability to pinch dorsal skin of toes)
searchTerms: unable to pinch skin on toes

common.symptomName: Skin thickening and fibrosis over affected limb
common.notes: Progressive skin changes due to lymph stasis
searchTerms: skin thickening and hardening over limb
fibrotic skin changes on affected limb

common.symptomName: Heaviness and discomfort in affected limb

occasional.notes: Thickened, scaly skin in chronic cases
Warty skin changes due to lymphatic obstruction

occasional.symptomName: Limited joint mobility in affected limb

searchTerms: fatigue localized to arm or leg

rare.notes: Rare malignant transformation in longstanding lymphedema
Rare lymphatic leakage into pleural or peritoneal spaces
Enlarged lymph nodes due to chronic inflammation

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during cellulitis episodes
imaging: Lymphoscintigraphy showing delayed or absent lymphatic drainage
Ultrasound demonstrating thickened subcutaneous tissue and absence of venous obstruction
genetic: No pathogenic variants identified in known hereditary lymphedema genes
other: Positive Stemmer sign on physical examination

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier age of onset (congenital or puberty)
History of surgery, trauma, infection, or malignancy
Localized to site of lymphatic injury
Symmetric lower limb fat deposition sparing feet

redFlags: Signs of infection such as fever and erythema
references: Rockson SG. Lymphedema. Am J Med. 2001;110(4):288-295.
